# models.scage { #falconage.models.scage }

```python
models.scage(cells, reference, *, grid=None, min_sites=20, binarise=0.5)
```

An age per cell, by profile likelihood over a grid of candidate ages.

## Parameters {.doc-section .doc-section-parameters}

| Name      | Type               | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                              | Default    |
|-----------|--------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|------------|
| cells     |                    | A :class:`~falconage.core.FalconData` of single cells: mostly NaN, with covered sites near 0 or 1.                                                                                                                                       | _required_ |
| grid      | np.ndarray \| None | Candidate ages. Defaults to a 0.5-year grid over the reference's own fitted range -- outside it the linear models are extrapolation.                                                                                                     | `None`     |
| min_sites | int                | A cell covering fewer informative sites than this gets NaN rather than a number. Twenty binary observations against a straight line is not an age estimate, and returning one anyway is how a per-cell table fills with confident noise. | `20`       |

## Returns {.doc-section .doc-section-returns}

| Name   | Type                                                                         | Description   |
|--------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------|
|        | One row per cell: the maximising age, how many informative sites it had, the |               |
|        | log-likelihood at the maximum, and the curvature-free width of the peak --   |               |
|        | the range of ages within 2 log-likelihood units, which is what says whether  |               |
|        | the cell had enough sites to distinguish anything.                           |               |
